title: Acceleration as a Derivative
short: a = dv/dt = d²x/dt², and zero velocity at an instant says nothing about the acceleration.
trouble: Students think an object with zero velocity at an instant must have zero acceleration there.

blocks.html: Acceleration and Its Sign defined acceleration as the rate at which velocity changes. With Velocity as a Derivative in hand, that rate is one more derivative.

$$\role{acceleration}{a}(t) = \dfrac{\role[tiny change in velocity]{velocity}{dv}}{\role[tiny time interval]{time}{dt}} = \dfrac{d^2\role{position}{x}}{\role{time}{dt^2}}.$$ Acceleration is the slope of the $v$–$t$ graph and the concavity of the $x$–$t$ graph. Its units are $(\text{m/s})/\text{s} = \text{m/s}^2$. The velocity at an instant and the acceleration at that instant are separate facts: either can be zero while the other is not.

The derivative at an instant depends on how a quantity is changing there, not on its value there. A velocity can pass through zero while it is changing quickly, like a ball at the top of its flight: just before the top its velocity is a little upward, just after it is a little downward. The change from $+$ to $-$ happens at a steady rate of $9.8\ \text{m/s}$ every second, so $a = -9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$ (up positive) right through the top.

blocks.name: ph-motion

opts.task: Pause at the top of the flight. Read the velocity and the acceleration there.

blocks.cap: A ball thrown up at 14.7 m/s. At the top (1.5 s) the $v$–$t$ line crosses zero, but its slope, the acceleration, is still $-9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$.

blocks.title: Differentiate twice
blocks.q: A particle has $x(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 5t$ (m, s). Find its velocity and acceleration at $t = 1\ \text{s}$.
steps: Both are negative: the particle moves in $-x$ and its velocity is becoming more negative, so it is speeding up.

blocks.title: At rest, but accelerating
blocks.q: For $x(t) = 2t^3 - 9t^2 + 12t$ (m, s), the particle is at rest at $t = 1\ \text{s}$. What is its acceleration then?
steps: The velocity is passing from positive to negative: the particle is turning around, and the nonzero acceleration is what turns it.

blocks.html: Thinking that zero velocity at an instant means zero acceleration. If the acceleration were also zero, the velocity would stay at zero and the object would sit still. A ball at the top of its throw doesn't hover. Check: look at the velocity a moment before and a moment after. If they differ, the acceleration is not zero.

head: $v$

What happens
blocks.cap: Same signs: speeding up. Opposite signs: slowing down.
